title: Functions of Travel Agencies and Tour Operations (Module 6A, lesson 21)
summary: Travel agents and tour operators account for about 70% of domestic and 90% of international tourist traffic. Their functions: marketing and publicity (brand building for destinations; they should be truthful), reservation of tickets (air, rail, ship, bus; now online through Global Distribution Systems), reservation of hotel rooms (earlier Computer Reservation Systems, CRS; online payment by internet banking or cards; room details must match reality), reservation of ground services (cars, coaches, caravans, guides, interpreters), selling cruise packages, preparing itineraries, designing and costing package tours, travel information and counselling, processing travel documents, travel insurance, currency exchange, research and development, training, event management (MICE), CSR and disaster preparedness.
## History of the Indian travel trade

Pallonji Katgara and Jamshedji Dastoor founded Jeena and Company (1900) and Jeena Tours and Travels in 1920, the first Indian-owned travel company, which joined Travel Corporation (India) in 1961. The Travel Agents Association of India (TAAI) was set up in 1951; earlier the trade was in the hands of Jeena, Lee and Muirhead India and N. Jamnadas and Co. A separate Ministry of Tourism and Civil Aviation was created under a cabinet minister in 1967. IRCTC was incorporated on 27 September 1999 as an extended arm of Indian Railways for catering and tourism and sells 'Railneer' bottled water.

Travel documents include passport, visa (an endorsement on a passport allowing entry, exit or stay for a specified time), health certificates, vaccination, insurance and foreign currency; agents process them and help clients avoid trouble. Research and development covers market research, itinerary feasibility, designing new packages, customer preference studies, branding and costing. Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) means contributing positively to society: training and skills, basic amenities in government schools, empowerment of women, community development and ensuring activities do not harm local people; destination sustainability needs it. Training covers handling guests, crisis management, soft skills, sales and marketing and updating technology skills.

Itinerary preparation, package design and costing are done by expert teams after familiarisation trips and feasibility studies. FIT is Foreign Independent Travel or Free Individual Traveller, GIT is Group Inclusive Tour and FAM is a Familiarisation tour (to check feasibility of an itinerary or promote it with destination promoters). Travel information (destinations, attractions, rates, accommodation, travel modes, formalities) turns 'lookers into bookers'.
## Organisations, insurance, currency, MICE and disasters

Coordination with the Ministry of Tourism (supreme policy maker), IATO, TAAI and global bodies: UFTAA (Universal Federation of Travel Agents Association), PATA (Pacific Asia Travel Association), WATA, UNWTO, IATA (International Air Transport Association) and WTTC. Travel insurance covers life, accident, medical treatment, baggage loss and trip cancellation. Foreign exchange service is permitted by the RBI and FEMA to registered agents at minimum commission. MICE packages are handled by large firms' MICE divisions. Disaster preparedness (cyclones, floods, earthquakes, terror) is vital: safety of visitors is the prime responsibility and agents coordinate with local disaster management teams.

vsa: Why is Corporate Social Responsibility important for travel agencies? (two points)
It ensures their activities do not harm local people and communities. It helps destination sustainability through training, school amenities and empowerment.
What is meant by FAM tour? Why is it conducted?
FAM is a familiarisation tour. It is conducted to check the feasibility of an itinerary or package and as a promotional method with destination promoters.
A visa is an endorsement on a passport that allows the holder to enter, leave or stay in a country for a specified period.
State two uses of travel insurance.
It gives security for personal and baggage losses. It covers life, accident, medical treatment and trip cancellation losses.
sa: Why is corporate social responsibility important? Explain in three points.

(i) Business should make a direct positive contribution to society. (ii) It supports training, basic amenities in government schools and empowerment of women. (iii) Destination sustainability is possible only when all stakeholders take social responsibility.
Explain any three functions of a travel agency (from this lesson).
(i) Marketing and publicity of packages and destinations. (ii) Reservation of tickets, hotel rooms and ground services. (iii) Travel information, document processing, insurance and currency exchange.
Explain the importance of itinerary preparation and package tour design (three points).
(i) Differentiated products help firms survive competition. (ii) Expert teams check feasibility through familiarisation trips. (iii) Costing and launching a package bring revenue and promote tourism.
Explain the importance of disaster preparedness for travel agencies (three points).

(i) Safety and security of visitors is the prime responsibility. (ii) Disasters such as floods, earthquakes and terror strikes are uncertain. (iii) Trained teams coordinate with local disaster management teams to prevent harm.
la: Explain the major functions of travel agencies and tour operators, in six points.

(i) Marketing and publicity of packages, destinations and attractions. (ii) Reservation of tickets, hotel rooms and ground services. (iii) Itinerary preparation, package designing and costing. (iv) Travel information and processing of passport, visa and other documents. (v) Travel insurance, currency exchange and organising MICE events. (vi) Research, training, CSR and disaster preparedness.
Explain the travel documents and the formalities travel agents handle for a foreign trip, in six points.

(i) Passport is the basic travel document. (ii) A visa is an endorsement allowing entry and stay for a period. (iii) Health certificates and vaccination are needed. (iv) Travel insurance covers life, baggage and cancellation. (v) Foreign currency is arranged within RBI and FEMA rules. (vi) Agents process these documents to avoid trouble or denied entry.
